name: Core v1.0
note: Edit the weights here to rotate Core. The next update writes the change to the ledger, entered at that day's open. Weights add up to 100 minus cash.
summary: Core v1.0 as set on Oct 30, 2026: an AI sleeve, a regime sleeve and a copper hedge, rotated by fixed rules.

holdings.thesis: The strongest large-cap trend on the screen. Q3 revenue +39% to $24.4B, and the FY guide raised a third time to $91–92B.
holdings.rotate_if: Drug-pricing legislation after the midterms, or GLP-1 demand stalls.

holdings.thesis: Energy was the top relative-strength sector with Brent near $112 on the US–Iran conflict. The majors' EPS was expected to roughly double year over year.
holdings.rotate_if: A peace deal drains the war premium and Brent drops below ~$95.

holdings.thesis: Q3 beat on Oct 30 on refining and output, with adjusted EPS reported at $5.28 vs about $4.89 expected. Direct oil exposure alongside XLE.
holdings.rotate_if: A peace deal drains the war premium and Brent drops below ~$95.

holdings.thesis: Customers kept their budgets (GOOGL $195–205B, AMZN ~$220B). Q3 guided to ~$108B with Rubin in production; supply, not demand, is the limit.
holdings.rotate_if: A hyperscaler cuts capex, or the ~Nov 17 guide disappoints.

holdings.thesis: Beat on Oct 29 (EPS $49.51) and guided Q2 to $55–57 EPS, about 6x annualized after a −25% month.
holdings.rotate_if: NAND contract prices stop rising. Also confirm how the venue handles the reported 8-for-1 split (single source).

holdings.thesis: Record $1.4B revenue, members +35% to 17.1M, the FY guide raised to $5.04B, and a preliminary 2027 outlook of $6.4B.
holdings.rotate_if: Credit losses rise, or 14-day funding stays above 30% APR.

holdings.thesis: Azure accelerated to +48%, guided to 49–50%. Revenue $92.3B (+19%) with capex below consensus: AI growth without the spending scare.
GMV +16%, revenue +13%, EPS $1.51 beat. The FY EPS guide of $6.25–6.30 is about 19.5x.
Q3 revenue $46.7B (+41%) at a 66.4% gross margin, with Q4 guided +58% YoY. It sold off on 2nm margin dilution.
holdings.rotate_if: Monthly sales roll over, or a Taiwan shock.

holdings.thesis: The whole chip stack, sold off on the spenders' fear. Breadth exposure to an AI rebound. Overlaps NVDA, AVGO, TSM and MU on purpose.
TrendForce sees memory at 68% of major cloud capex in 2027. FQ1 guided to $61.5B / $38.15 EPS; 2027 HBM largely sold out.
Biotech M&A on pace for its best year since before Covid ($106B across 201 deals).
Near its record, and China paid a record $205/t premium, a sign of physical tightness.
holdings.rotate_if: A China demand slump or a tariff shock.

holdings.thesis: Record Q3: EPS $2.02, futures and options volume +31%, energy revenue +26%. Earns on volatility.
+25% in 6 months. Guides +9–11% revenue with mid-teens iPhone growth. Reports Nov 2.
holdings.rotate_if: The December-quarter guide gets hit by memory costs.

holdings.thesis: A defensive compounder in an uptrend: September comps +11.4%, digital +19%.
Owner's pick, held outside the score rule. Q2 revenue rose 92% to $7.8B on Starlink, with a $541M loss driven by xAI. Fast growth, a very high valuation, and the most volatile name here.
holdings.rotate_if: Starlink growth stalls, xAI spending keeps widening losses, or the December lockup brings heavy insider selling.
